cards.explanation: The news is that the city has been taken. In the twelfth year of the exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a fugitive from Jerusalem comes to Ezekiel and reports, "The city has been taken!" (Ezekiel 33:21). Ezekiel is the prophet telling this. That's a short sentence, friends, and I think it landed like a dropped tray of cookies.

The answer is mouth. The evening before the man arrives, the hand of the LORD is upon Ezekiel (Ezekiel 33:22). The text says He opened Ezekiel's mouth before the man came in the morning. Ezekiel is no longer mute.

The answer is that there are many of them. The people in the ruins say, "Abraham was only one man, yet he possessed the land. But we are many; surely the land has been given to us as a possession." (Ezekiel 33:24). Their reasoning is that if one man got it, a crowd surely does. Numbers sound strong, friends, but numbers aren't a promise.

God asks whether they should possess the land. After naming the blood, the idols and the shed blood, God asks, "Should you then possess the land?" (Ezekiel 33:25). The people said the land was theirs because they were many. God puts their way of living next to that claim and asks.

The answer is that they will die by plague. God says those in the strongholds and caves "…will die by plague." (Ezekiel 33:27). Sword for the ruins, wild animals for the open field, plague for the strongholds and caves. This is a heavy part, friends.

The answer is True. God says, "The mountains of Israel will become desolate, so that no one will pass through." (Ezekiel 33:28). He also says He will make the land a desolate waste. It's a heavy picture, and I think it's okay to just sit with it for a moment.

The answer is False. God says He will make the land a desolate waste "…because of all the abominations they have committed." (Ezekiel 33:29). The text says they did wrong, friends. It names idols, shed blood and detestable acts (Ezekiel 33:25-26).

The answer is that they will know He is the LORD. God says, "Then they will know that I am the LORD…" (Ezekiel 33:29). It comes when He has made the land a desolate waste because of the abominations. The whole thing ends with them knowing who He is.

The answer is "Come and hear the message from the LORD." God says the people speak to each other, "Come and hear the message that has come from the LORD!" (Ezekiel 33:30). They say it near the city walls and in the doorways of their houses. Ezekiel's name is getting around like a rumor about free cookies.

The answer is that they don't put his words into practice. God says, "…they do not put them into practice." (Ezekiel 33:31). They come as usual, sit down and hear Ezekiel's words, friends. Then the words stay in the room and don't follow them home.

The answer is False. God says, "Although they express love with their mouths, their hearts pursue dishonest gain." (Ezekiel 33:31). Their mouths say one thing and their hearts chase another. It's like someone who says "love you!" with a big smile while quietly reaching for your wallet.

The answer is a singer of love songs. God says Ezekiel is to them "…like a singer of love songs with a beautiful voice, who skillfully plays an instrument." (Ezekiel 33:32). The verse also says they hear his words but do not put them into practice. That's the part that matters, friends.

The answer is prophet. God says, "So when it comes to pass—and surely it will come—then they will know that a prophet has been among them." (Ezekiel 33:33). The word will come to pass. Then they'll know a prophet was right there with them.
